solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Final year note about work by Keats

parts.note: the final part of something is its end
MI is the third note of the sol-fa scale
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A student's last-year assignment, a note written on a Keats poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote a long narrative poem named after the shepherd loved by the moon goddess Selene.

clue.text: Pray to God Herod pulls round

indicators.note: pulled round, the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A plea to heaven as the tyrant Herod turns about.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation appealing for divine help, a heartfelt prayer in a crisis.

clue.text: Waving baton is cue for leader of orchestra

indicators.note: a waving baton is in motion, so its letters, with the rest, are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A conductor's waving baton signals the orchestra to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz pianist led his own famous big band for decades, a swing orchestra bandleader.

clue.text: Smooth, slippery rock enclosing lake

indicators.note: the rock wraps around the lake, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Rock is Gibraltar, shortened to Gib
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A smooth, slippery boulder surrounding a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib talker is smooth and slippery, fluent but insincere and hard to pin down.

clue.text: Old coins stripped from holy city in Israel

indicators.note: the coins are taken off the word for holy, one at each end

parts.note: holy means sacred
s and d were the shilling and penny of pre-decimal British money

explanation.surface: Ancient coins being taken away from a sacred city in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: Pre-1971 British money was pounds, shillings and pence (L s d); 'stripped from' removes S and D from either end of SACRED.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Crusader port is a coastal city in northern Israel, also called Akko.

clue.text: Dickens "ordinary"? Idiot!

parts.note: Boz was the pen name Charles Dickens used for his early sketches
O for ordinary, as in the old British O level exams

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at Dickens, branded ordinary, calling him an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: O level was the 'ordinary' school exam in Britain, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a clownish fool or buffoon, an American slang word for a stupid person.

clue.text: Get away from it all on England's southern headland

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for England
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A holiday retreat on a promontory on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off for a holiday break from daily routine is to make a getaway, a synonym.

clue.text: Entirely independent new group getting platinum from Africa

parts.note: the rock band Toto had a platinum-selling hit single called Africa

explanation.surface: A band, new and independent, earning platinum discs with African music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Africa' looks like the continent, but it is the band's 1982 hit record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, completely, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sport embraced by all across Europe

indicators.note: the word is held inside the run of letters of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A game popular in every country across the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A team game played with netted sticks, originally from Native American tradition.

clue.text: Composer moving contents out of Brondesbury Road

indicators.note: the insides of both words are cleared out, leaving only their end letters

explanation.surface: A musician moving house, clearing belongings from a flat on a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: Brondesbury is a district of north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was the great Tudor English composer of church and keyboard music.

clue.text: Aristo breaking bread with old Madame Cholet after cycling?

indicators.note: the flatbread is broken open to take the other pieces inside

parts.note: naan is Indian flatbread, also spelt nan

indicators.note: the letters of the creature's name are rotated, the front moved round to the back

parts.note: Madame Cholet is the cook among the Wombles, furry creatures of a British children's TV series

explanation.surface: A posh lady snapping a loaf with an old French housekeeper after a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Cholet sounds like a real Frenchwoman, but she is the cook of the Wombles, and 'after cycling' rotates her kind's name by moving its first three letters to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is a member of the aristocracy, and this is a lady of noble rank.

clue.text: Julius is in Delaware a bit

indicators.note: the setter's words are placed inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Delaware
Julius is the setter, so from his own mouth this is I'm

explanation.surface: The setter announces he is in Delaware for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym stands for I or ME; here 'Julius is' is I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-cent coin is a small amount, as in 'not worth a dime', so a little bit.

clue.text: It's a stick-up job

parts.note: it suggests a robbery, but means a person whose work is pasting notices up on walls

explanation.walkthrough: 'stick-up' looks like an armed hold-up; it is literally sticking posters up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to paste advertising notices onto hoardings does literally stick things up.

clue.text: Fast or, at first, slowly?

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the little word is taken

explanation.surface: A puzzled question: should one go quickly or, to begin with, slowly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, the opposite of the definition, but it is a period of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction tells players to perform at a slow tempo.

clue.text: Like Lord Copper to continue to obstruct the legal profession

indicators.note: the legal profession blocks the middle of the phrase by sitting inside it

parts.note: to press on is to keep going
the Bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: A peer keeps on blocking lawyers, like a meddling magnate.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Copper is the newspaper tycoon in Evelyn Waugh's novel Scoop. The definition describes the type he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's Lord Copper is the archetypal powerful newspaper proprietor, a magnate of the media.

clue.text: Knight making a dash, clutching precious grail

indicators.note: the first rearranged pair holds the second inside it
the letters are made into something new, worked into another order
the grail's letters are treated preciously, fussed over into a new order

explanation.surface: A knight sprinting off, gripping the prized Holy Grail.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'making' rearranges 'a dash' and 'precious' rearranges 'grail', and the second sits inside the first between its opening S and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Galahad was the purest of King Arthur's Round Table knights, who achieved the Grail.

clue.text: Independence movement taking afternoon break

indicators.note: the party takes the single letter into its middle

parts.note: the SNP, the Scottish National Party, campaigns for Scottish independence
A is short for afternoon, as in p.m. or a. abbreviations

explanation.surface: Political campaigners stopping for an afternoon tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig or bone will snap, which is to break suddenly with a crack.

clue.text: Royal beard treatment carried out by daughter, 19?

definitions.text: Royal beard treatment carried out by daughter, 19?

parts.words: Royal beard treatment carried out by daughter, 19
parts.note: daughter is D and 19 is the Lothario, so together they name the admiral who scorched a royal beard

explanation.walkthrough: D (daughter) before RAKE (19) gives DRAKE: Sir Francis Drake's 1587 raid on Cadiz was said to have 'singed the King of Spain's beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch lightly at the tips, which is what Drake did figuratively to Philip of Spain's whiskers.

clue.text: Lothario found in belly of Nordic sea-monster

indicators.note: only the inside of the monster is kept, its first and last letters dropped

parts.note: the kraken is a giant sea monster of Norse legend

explanation.surface: A womaniser swallowed by a legendary Scandinavian sea beast.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario is a seducer of women, from a play by Rowe; a rake is a dissolute ladies' man.

clue.text: Running amok, Ruth Gordon bought it here

indicators.note: running amok, the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Ruth Gordon, the actress, going berserk on a shopping spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth Gordon' looks like the actress's name, but Gordon is General Gordon; 'bought it' is slang for was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: General Charles Gordon was killed in 1885 when the Mahdi's forces took the Sudanese capital.

clue.text: Rich American pursuing Miranda's father

indicators.note: the American follows behind, so it comes after

parts.note: Prospero is Miranda's father in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: A wealthy American chasing after a young woman's father.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: wealthy, well-off and thriving financially.

clue.text: He gets up for work, often burdened by shingles

definitions.text: He gets up for work, often burdened by shingles

parts.words: He gets up for work, often burdened by shingles
parts.note: it reads as a sufferer of the painful rash, but describes a tradesman who climbs up carrying wooden roof tiles

explanation.walkthrough: Shingles is a painful viral rash, but also wooden tiles laid on roofs; 'gets up' is climbing up a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who climbs onto buildings to lay tiles or shingles on the top.

clue.text: Wasting a billion in two instalments, ruin Dutch football side

indicators.note: the billion is squandered, taken out of the word
the two letters go separately, one from the front and one from the middle

parts.note: banjax is Irish and British slang meaning to ruin or wreck
bn is the standard abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A club squandering a fortune paid in two parts, ruining itself.
explanation.walkthrough: BANJAX loses B and N, taken from two separate places.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax of Amsterdam is the most famous club in the Netherlands' top football league.

clue.text: Patience? I manage recovery, initially being in non-responsive state

indicators.note: the inner pieces are put inside the unconscious state

parts.note: a coma is a state of deep unconsciousness
to cope is to manage

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A patient in a coma, waiting stoically for a recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' looks like the virtue, but it is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience is an example of a light, humorous operetta.

clue.text: Goodness regularly seen in Miss Mary?

indicators.note: every other letter of the two words is taken, starting from the second

explanation.surface: A prim exclamation from a schoolmistress named Mary?
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise, much like saying 'well, well'.

clue.text: Probabilities of party upset gutted Democrats

indicators.note: in a down entry the party is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the insides are removed, leaving only the end letters

explanation.surface: Polling chances after a party is upset and Democrats are devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds express the likelihood of an outcome, so the plural means chances.

clue.text: City head office office office?

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A bewildered repetition of the word for a company's main workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two words repeat the preceding one, as a reverberation would.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound repeated by reflection, which is how 'office office' trails after the first word.

clue.text: Get her away from 8's falsetto

indicators.note: the two words are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: 8 across means entirely, which is another word for altogether

explanation.surface: Telling a woman to leave a high-pitched singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alto names the high male voice produced in falsetto, the countertenor range.

clue.text: Victoria (the Queen) & Albert (husband) gallery

parts.note: V for Victoria
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
the ampersand is read as and
A for Albert, as in the V&A

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria and her husband Albert, recalled by a London museum gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed open porch along the side of a house, also called a gallery.

clue.text: Pop a question that's a bit unclear

indicators.note: only a fragment of the phrase's run of letters is used

explanation.surface: Asking an awkward question that is somewhat vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to understand, or not letting light through, is obscure.
